mainTopic: Preparing food on יום טוב when part of it is not for Jews: shared animals and dough, dog-dough, and food for soldiers
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about sprinkling blood when the meat cannot be eaten that day. It implies the sprinkling is only acceptable after the fact, which fits רבא but is difficult for רבה בר רב הונא. The גמרא admits the difficulty, then suggests that the rabbis were stricter about שבות on שבת than on יום טוב. Next, רב הונא permits slaughtering on יום טוב an animal half owned by a גוי. He dodges רב אויא סבא's comparison to נדרים ונדבות, and later explains to his son that he was too tired to reason it out. The real difference: you cannot get even a כזית of meat without slaughtering the whole animal, but offerings are eaten from God's table. רב חסדא adds that shared dough may not be baked, because it can be split during kneading. Dog-dough that shepherds eat is explained as a case where a נבלה is already on hand for the dogs. Finally, רב הונא allows baking soldiers' bread if a Jewish child may eat from it. The גמרא challenges him from the story of שמעון התימני and the calf. The answers lead to a dispute between תנאים about whether one may cook for animals on יום טוב, and that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ending of the ברייתא: the offering is accepted, and the fats are burned at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא. It says that in a case where the meat could not be eaten that day, the offering is still accepted, on condition that the אימורין are burned in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is accepted, on condition that he burns the sacrificial parts in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא that it is about to use as evidence. This line is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes a case where the blood was already sprinkled, even though the meat could not be eaten that day. It says the offering still 'works' (הורצה), and the fats are simply burned later, at night. The exact wording here matters, because the next step draws an inference from it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was accepted; the offering achieved its purpose
The fats and parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: It is accepted,
phrases.notes: This is the tail end of a ברייתא that started on the previous page; the case is where the blood was already sprinkled.

phrases.english: on condition that he burns the sacrificial parts in the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּרְצָה, עַל מְנָת לְהַקְטִיר אֵימוּרִין לָעֶרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous page
steps.raayaObject: Whether sprinkling the blood is allowed from the outset when the meat cannot be eaten

steps.title: Inference: only after the fact, not from the start
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'if he sprinkled', the גמרא infers that sprinkling is only acceptable after the fact (דיעבד), not from the outset (לכתחלה).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he sprinkled' means: after the fact, yes; from the start, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely and pulls out a hidden implication. The phrase 'if he sprinkled' suggests that he should not have done so in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never says outright that sprinkling is forbidden. But the phrasing 'if he did it, it works' implies it is only bearable after the fact. So the inference is that, ideally, one should not sprinkle in this situation.

keyTerms.meaning: He sprinkled (the blood on the מזבח)
After the fact; once it has already been done
From the outset; ideally, before acting

phrases.english: If he sprinkled — after the fact, yes,
from the start — no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם זָרַק, דִּיעֲבַד — אִין, לְכַתְּחִלָּה — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the ברייתא just quoted
steps.raayaObject: That sprinkling in this case is not allowed לכתחלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The phrase 'אם זרק' in the ברייתא

steps.title: This fits רבא but is difficult for רבה בר רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The inference matches רבא's view. It contradicts רבה בר רב הונא, whose position seems to allow sprinkling from the outset.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבא it works well. But according to רבה בר רב הונא it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא aims the inference at the two earlier opinions. It fits one of them and creates a problem for the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's view agrees that one should not sprinkle לכתחלה here, so the ברייתא supports him. רבה בר רב הונא's earlier ruling seems to permit it even from the start, and that clashes with the ברייתא's 'only after the fact' wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; it makes sense according to...

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rava it works well,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא קַשְׁיָא!
phrases.english: but according to Rabba bar Rav Huna it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרָבָא נִיחָא, אֶלָּא לְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the inference from the ברייתא to the two earlier opinions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies sprinkling is only acceptable דיעבד, while his view seems to allow it לכתחלה

steps.title: The גמרא admits: it is indeed difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concedes that the question against רבה בר רב הונא stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is indeed difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא openly admits that this is a real problem for רבה בר רב הונא. The next step still offers a possible way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating the single word 'קשיא' is the גמרא's way of saying 'yes, this is a real problem'. It is weaker than a full refutation (תיובתא), and step 5 goes on to suggest an answer that would save רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.confusionAlert: The same word קשיא appears twice in a row. The first one asks the question. The second one is the גמרא agreeing that the question is real.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the previous קשיא as unresolved
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא remains a difficulty for רבה בר רב הונא

steps.title: שבות on שבת is different from שבות on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a way to save רבה בר רב הונא. The ברייתא is talking about שבת, and the rabbis were stricter with their decrees on שבת than on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: a rabbinic prohibition of שבת is different from a rabbinic prohibition of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after admitting the difficulty, the גמרא suggests a possible answer. The ברייתא's strictness applies to שבת, while רבה בר רב הונא was speaking about יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's 'only after the fact' rule reflects a שבות of שבת, which the rabbis treated more strictly. רבה בר רב הונא can then say that on יום טוב, where rabbinic decrees are more lenient, sprinkling is allowed even from the start. So the two sources don't clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (introduces another answer)
A rabbinic prohibition of activity on שבת or יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא implies sprinkling is only acceptable דיעבד. That is a difficulty for רבה בר רב הונא, but it can be answered: the rabbis were stricter about שבות on שבת than on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאנֵי שְׁבוּת שַׁבָּת מִשְּׁבוּת יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: A rabbinic decree of Shabbat is different from a rabbinic decree of a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: שָׁאנֵי שְׁבוּת שַׁבָּת מִשְּׁבוּת יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible resolution after the difficulty was conceded
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (שבת vs. יום טוב)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's strictness applies equally to יום טוב
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about שבת, where the rabbis were stricter, so רבה בר רב הונא's lenient ruling for יום טוב stands

steps.title: רב אויא סבא asks about an animal half owned by a גוי
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא סבא asks רב הונא whether one may slaughter on יום טוב an animal that is half owned by a גוי and half by a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא סבא asked רב הונא: an animal that is half a גוי's and half a Jew's, may one slaughter it on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב אויא סבא asks a practical question about a jointly owned animal on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking and slaughtering on יום טוב are only allowed for food for Jews. Here, half the animal belongs to a גוי, so the question is whether that half makes the slaughter forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of it belongs to a non-Jew

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִנֵּיהּ רַב אַוְיָא סָבָא מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Avya the Elder asked Rav Huna:
An animal, half of which belongs to a gentile
and half of which belongs to a Jew,
what is the law about slaughtering it on a Festival?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִנֵּיהּ רַב אַוְיָא סָבָא מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion, related to the earlier theme of slaughter and offerings on יום טוב
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether partial ownership by a גוי forbids slaughtering the animal on יום טוב

steps.title: רב הונא: it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that it is permitted to slaughter the jointly owned animal on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a short, clear ruling: one may slaughter the shared animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא gives no reason here. The missing reason is exactly what opens the door to the next challenge.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Slaughtering the jointly owned animal on יום טוב is permitted

steps.title: What about נדרים ונדבות?
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא challenges: how is this different from נדרים ונדבות, which may not be offered on יום טוב?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: and what is the difference between this and נדרים ונדבות?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא pushes back by comparing the shared animal to voluntary offerings, which are forbidden to slaughter on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדר or נדבה also looks 'split': part goes to the מזבח, and part is eaten by people. If those are forbidden on יום טוב, why should an animal partly owned by a גוי be any different?

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difference between...?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי מָה בֵּין זֶה
phrases.english: He said to him: And what is the difference between this
and vow-offerings and gift-offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה בֵּין זֶה לִנְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's permission to slaughter the shared animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נדרים ונדבות are also partly 'not for the Jew's eating' and are forbidden, so the shared animal should be forbidden too

steps.title: רב הונא changes the subject: 'A raven is flying!'
steps.stepSummary: Instead of answering, רב הונא distracts רב אויא by pointing at a raven flying by.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: a raven is flying!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא avoids the question by changing the subject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a real answer to the challenge. It is a way of pushing the question off. The next steps explain why he did this and then give the real answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A raven is flying (said to distract)

phrases.english: He said to him: A raven flies!
phrases.notes: He's changing the subject on purpose, so he doesn't have to answer right now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Evades the challenge instead of answering it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Does not engage the challenge at all
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: None; this is an evasion, and the real answer comes later

steps.title: רבה questions his father: isn't he the great scholar you praised?
steps.stepSummary: After רב אויא leaves, רבה, son of רב הונא, asks why his father brushed off a man he himself had praised as great.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he left, רבה his son said to him: isn't this רב אויא סבא, whom you used to praise to us as a great man?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is gently criticizing his father for how he treated רב אויא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not about the הלכה but about רב הונא's behavior. If רב אויא is a great scholar, why not give him a real answer?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי נְפַק אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: When he left, Rabba his son said to him:
Isn't this Rav Avya the Elder
whom Master used to praise to us,
phrases.notes: 'Master' means רב הונא himself; his son is speaking to him respectfully.

phrases.english: that he is a great man?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי נְפַק אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's evasion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: You yourself called him a great man, so he deserved a real answer

steps.title: רב הונא explains: I was exhausted, and the question needed real thought
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says he was worn out that day and the question required careful reasoning, so he could not answer properly on the spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: and what could I do for him? Today I am 'Sustain me with flagons, comfort me with apples', and he asked me something that needs a reason.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself. He wasn't being disrespectful; he was simply too tired to work through a hard question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By quoting the פסוק, רב הונא describes himself as weak and in need of support. He admits the question was a good one that required a reasoned answer, which tells us a real distinction is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: What could I do for him?
Sustain me with flagons (a phrase describing weakness)

phrases.english: He said to him: And what should I have done for him?
Today I am
'Sustain me with flagons,
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 2:5 — he means he's worn out and needs propping up.

phrases.english: comfort me with apples,'
and he asked me something that requires reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's criticism
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא was being dismissive of a great scholar
steps.terutzMaskana: He was exhausted, and the question needed careful reasoning he couldn't give right then

steps.title: So what is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the actual difference is between the shared animal and נדרים ונדבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the halachic question and sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב הונא admitted the question needs a reason, the גמרא now supplies one. This line only opens the explanation.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the unanswered challenge from step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The distinction between a shared animal and נדרים ונדבות

steps.title: You can't get a כזית without slaughtering, but offerings come from God's table
steps.stepSummary: The shared animal is permitted because even a כזית of meat for the Jew requires slaughtering the whole animal. נדרים ונדבות are forbidden because whoever eats them, even the כהנים, eats from the 'table of the Most High'.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal half a גוי's and half a Jew's may be slaughtered on יום טוב, because you can't have even a כזית of meat without slaughtering. But נדרים ונדבות may not be slaughtered on יום טוב, because when the כהנים receive their share, they receive it from the table of the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason that separates the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the shared animal, the Jew truly needs to slaughter the animal to get his own meat, and there is no way to slaughter just 'his half'. With נדרים ונדבות, the whole animal belongs to God, and the people who eat are like guests at His table. So that slaughter is not for people's food on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's volume, the minimum amount of food
The table of the Most High; God's table

steps.whatToRemember: A shared animal (half גוי, half Jew) may be slaughtered on יום טוב, because you can't get any meat without slaughtering the whole animal. נדרים ונדבות are forbidden, because the entire offering belongs to God and people eat 'from His table', not their own.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: what matters is whose food the slaughter is really for. Owning an animal jointly with a גוי is different from an animal that belongs entirely to הקדש.

phrases.aramaic: בְּהֵמָה חֶצְיָהּ שֶׁל גּוֹי וְחֶצְיָהּ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: An animal, half of which belongs to a gentile and half to a Jew,
may be slaughtered on a Festival,
because it is impossible to have an olive-bulk of meat
without slaughtering.
But vow-offerings and gift-offerings
it is forbidden to slaughter them on a Festival,
because the priests, when they receive their share —
they receive it from the table of the Most High.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִכְזַיִת בָּשָׂר בְּלֹא שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 and resolves the challenge of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A shared animal is permitted because a Jew can't get any meat without full slaughter. נדרים ונדבות are forbidden because they are wholly God's, and those who eat receive from His table.

steps.title: A shared animal may be slaughtered, but shared dough may not be baked
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that an animal half-owned by a גוי may be slaughtered on יום טוב. Dough half-owned by a גוי may not be baked, because it can be split apart while kneading.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: an animal that is half a גוי's and half a Jew's may be slaughtered on יום טוב, because you cannot get even a כזית of meat without slaughtering. But dough that is half a גוי's and half a Jew's may not be baked on יום טוב, because he can divide it during kneading.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a clear rule that compares two shared items, an animal and a dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking on יום טוב is only allowed for Jewish needs. With an animal, the Jew's share cannot be separated out: to get any meat at all, the whole animal must be slaughtered. Dough can be split before baking, so the גוי's half is extra work for a גוי, and baking it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of it belongs to a non-Jew
An olive's volume, the smallest meaningful amount of food

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the test that the rest of the sugya argues over: is it possible to separate out the Jew's portion?

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
An animal, half of which belongs to a gentile
and half of which belongs to a Jew —
it is permitted to slaughter it on יום טוב,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִכְזַיִת בָּשָׂר בְּלֹא שְׁחִיטָה.
phrases.english: because it is impossible to get even an olive's worth of meat without slaughtering.
Dough, half of which belongs to a gentile
and half of which belongs to a Jew —
it is forbidden to bake it on יום טוב,
because he is able to divide it during the kneading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reasoning in step 13 (you need the whole animal for even a כזית) and adds a contrasting case of dough.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shared animal may be slaughtered on יום טוב because it can't be divided. Shared dough may not be baked because it can be divided during kneading.

steps.title: An objection from dog-dough that shepherds also eat
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר חנילאי quotes a משנה: dough made for dogs, if shepherds eat it too, counts as real bread. One of its rules is that it may be baked on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר חנילאי objected: dough for dogs, when shepherds also eat from it, is obligated in חלה. It can be used for an עירוב and a שיתוף. One makes a ברכה over it and makes a זימון over it. It may be baked on יום טוב, and a person fulfills his מצה obligation with it on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that looks like it clashes with רב חסדא. This step quotes the source; the next step points out exactly where the clash is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This dough is partly for people (the shepherds) and partly for dogs, much like dough that is partly a Jew's and partly a גוי's. Even so, the משנה says it may be baked on יום טוב. That doesn't fit רב חסדא's rule against baking dough when only part of it is for permitted eating.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן
Making a זימון (the group call to Grace after Meals)

phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Chanilai objected:
Dough for dogs,
when the shepherds eat from it —
is obligated in חלה,
and one may make an עירוב with it, and a שיתוף with it,
phrases.notes: An עירוב joins courtyards; a שיתוף joins an alleyway. Both let you carry on שבת.

phrases.english: and one makes a blessing over it, and one makes a זימון over it,
and it may be baked on יום טוב,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: and a person fulfills his obligation with it on פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that seems to contradict רב חסדא's ban on baking shared dough.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that dough which can be divided may not be baked on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dog-dough is only partly for people, yet the משנה allows baking all of it on יום טוב.

steps.title: Why not just split the dog-dough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem: the dog-dough could also be divided during kneading, so why may it be baked?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it allowed? He could divide it during the kneading!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the objection by applying רב חסדא's own reasoning to the dog-dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רב חסדא's logic, the baker should split off the dogs' share and bake only the people's share. The משנה lets him bake everything together, which seems to go against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: And why? (a challenge to a ruling)

phrases.english: And why?
But surely he is able to divide it during the kneading!
phrases.notes: These are רב חסדא's own words from step 14, now turned against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? וְהָא אֶפְשָׁר לֵיהּ לְמִפְלְגַהּ בְּלֵישָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the exact contradiction between the משנה in step 15 and רב חסדא in step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dog-dough can be divided just like shared dough, yet it may be baked.

steps.title: Dog-dough is different: the dogs might get a carcass instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that dog-dough is a special case. Since the dogs could be fed a נבלה instead, all of the dough might end up eaten by people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Dog-dough is different, since it is possible to satisfy the dogs with a נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא by showing why dog-dough is a different kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With shared dough, the גוי's half really does belong to the גוי. With dog-dough, nothing is fixed: if an animal dies, the dogs eat its carcass and the people eat all the bread. Because of this possibility ("הואיל"), the whole dough counts as fit for people.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: Dog-dough is different,
since it is possible to satisfy them with a carcass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (חילוק), based on הואיל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dog-dough is the same as shared dough and should be divided.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dog-dough might all be eaten by people, so all of it counts as people-food.

steps.title: Does רב חסדא even accept the idea of הואיל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב חסדא accepts הואיל at all. It points to a known dispute: about someone who bakes on יום טוב for a weekday, רב חסדא says he gets מלקות and רבה says he doesn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רב חסדא hold of "since"? It was stated: one who bakes on יום טוב for a weekday — רב חסדא said he is flogged; רבה said he is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It brings a different dispute that suggests רב חסדא rejects הואיל reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 17 depends on הואיל, a "what could happen" argument. In the baking dispute, רב חסדא gives מלקות to someone who bakes for after יום טוב, so he does not excuse it because of what might happen. That suggests he doesn't use הואיל, which would make the step 17 answer unusable for him.

keyTerms.meaning: On יום טוב for use on a weekday

phrases.english: But does Rav Chisda accept "since"?
But wasn't it stated:
one who bakes on יום טוב for a weekday —
Rav Chisda said: he is flogged,
Rabbah said: he is not flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַב חִסְדָּא הוֹאִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הואיל answer from step 17 by asking whether it fits רב חסדא's own views.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using הואיל to explain רב חסדא's position.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא's ruling that the baker gets מלקות suggests he rejects הואיל reasoning, so the answer in step 17 can't work for him.

steps.title: רב חסדא does not accept 'since', so the dog-dough answer fails for him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the dispute it just mentioned. רב חסדא says the baker gets מלקות because he does not accept הואיל. רבה says he does not get מלקות because he does accept הואיל. So the dog-dough answer, which relied on הואיל, cannot fit רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: he gets lashes. We do not say: 'Since guests might drop in on him, the bread is fit for him on יום טוב, so even now it counts as fit for him.' רבה said: he does not get lashes, because we do say 'since'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind the dispute from step 18. This finishes the challenge: רב חסדא himself rejects הואיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה reasons that guests might come, so whatever you bake could be eaten today, and the baking counts as permitted. רב חסדא does not accept that kind of 'maybe' reasoning, so the baker deserves lashes. The step 17 answer about dog-dough ('the dogs might get a נבלה') was exactly a הואיל argument, so it cannot be used to defend רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since': since something could happen, we treat it as if it already counts
Guests might happen to come to him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבה (the one who accepts הואיל here) with רב חסדא (the one who rejects it). The whole challenge depends on רב חסדא being the one who rejects it.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: he gets lashes,
we do not say "since
guests might happen to come to him, it is fit for him,
so now too it counts as fit for him."
Rabba said: he does not get lashes,
we do say "since."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: לוֹקֶה, לָא אָמְרִינַן הוֹאִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge begun in step 18 by spelling out each side's reasoning.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 17 (dog-dough is different because of הואיל)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא rejects הואיל elsewhere, so an answer built on הואיל cannot defend his ruling.

steps.title: New answer: the shepherds already have a carcass for the dogs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the הואיל answer. It now explains the dog-dough case as one where the owner already has a נבלה, so the dogs will surely be fed with it and the people will surely eat the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, don't say 'since it is possible.' Say instead that this is a case where he already has a נבלה, so he can certainly satisfy the dogs with the נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back its earlier answer and gives a new one that does not need הואיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the dogs only 'might' get a נבלה, and that is a הואיל argument. Now the נבלה is already there, so it is practically certain the dogs eat it and the dough goes to people. This is not a 'maybe' anymore, so it fits even רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: To satisfy (appease) them, meaning the dogs

steps.whatToRemember: The dog-dough may be baked on יום טוב according to רב חסדא only because a נבלה is already on hand. It is not because it 'might' become food for people.

phrases.english: Rather: do not say "since it is possible,"
phrases.notes: This takes back the step 17 answer: since the dogs might be fed a נבלה.

phrases.english: rather, it is a case where he has a carcass,
so it is certainly possible to satisfy them with the carcass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 18-19 by replacing the step 17 answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) so that it no longer depends on הואיל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dog-dough is permitted only because the dogs might be fed a נבלה (הואיל).
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is where a נבלה is already available, so it is certain the dough will be eaten by people.

steps.title: רב הונא is asked about baking the soldiers' bread on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: Villagers were forced to supply flour and bread to the army. People ask רב הונא whether they may bake it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב הונא: villagers who had to supply flour for the soldiers. May they bake it on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. A practical question is brought to רב הונא about baking on יום טוב for non-Jewish soldiers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baking on יום טוב is allowed only for food Jews may eat that day. The bread here is meant for the soldiers, so the question is whether it counts as food for Jews at all.

phrases.english: They asked Rav Huna:
these villagers
who were forced to supply flour for the soldiers,
what is the law about baking it on Yom Tov?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related question about baking on יום טוב for non-Jews.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May Jews bake on יום טוב bread that they must hand over to non-Jewish soldiers?

steps.title: רב הונא: it depends on whether the soldiers mind a child eating some
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that if the soldiers don't mind when a Jewish child is given some of the bread, every loaf counts as fit for a Jew, and baking is allowed. If they do mind, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: we check. If they give a child bread from it and the soldiers don't mind, then every single loaf is fit for a child, and it is allowed. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question with a test: do the soldiers care if a child gets some bread?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If any loaf could end up with a Jewish child, then each loaf is real food for a Jew on יום טוב, so baking it is allowed. If the soldiers are strict about their bread, none of it is for Jews, and baking it is plain forbidden work.

phrases.english: He said (to them): we check:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: if they give bread from it to a child
and they don't mind,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the soldiers. The question is whether they are bothered when some bread goes to a Jewish child.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא חַזְיָא לְיָנוֹקָא, וּשְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: each and every loaf is fit for a child, and it is permitted.
And if not, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Baking is allowed only if the soldiers don't mind a Jewish child getting some of the bread, because then each loaf is fit for a Jew.

steps.title: The story of שמעון התימני and the calf for the raiders
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב הונא. שמעון התימני missed the study hall at night, and explained to רבי יהודה בן בבא that a raiding troop came and the townspeople slaughtered a calf to feed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: there was a story with שמעון התימני, who didn't come to the study hall last night. In the morning רבי יהודה בן בבא found him and asked: why didn't you come last night? He answered: a search troop came to our city and wanted to plunder the whole city. We slaughtered a calf for them, fed them, and sent them away in peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רב הונא's lenient ruling by starting to tell a ברייתא story. The point of the challenge comes in the lines after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is about preparing food on יום טוב for non-Jews, which is the same topic as רב הונא's ruling. So far we only hear what שמעון התימני did; רבי יהודה בן בבא's reaction, which is what creates the problem, comes next.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
There was an incident with Shimon the Timnite
who did not come last night to the study hall.
phrases.notes: The night in the story is a יום טוב night. That is why it connects to our topic.

phrases.english: In the morning, Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava found him,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and said to him: why
did you not come last night to the study hall?
He said to him: a search troop came to our city,
and wanted to plunder the whole city,
so we slaughtered a calf for them and fed them,
and sent them away in peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge from a ברייתא against רב הונא's ruling in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that one may bake for soldiers on יום טוב if a Jewish child could also eat from it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The setup is still in progress: a ברייתא about preparing food on יום טוב for non-Jews is being quoted, and its continuation will show the problem with רב הונא's leniency.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בבא's response: 'For you, not for non-Jews'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בבא tells שמעון התימני that what the town saved may have been cancelled out by its sin, because יום טוב cooking is allowed only 'for you', not for non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I wonder if your gain was not cancelled out by your loss. For the Torah said: 'For you', and not for non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step is finished here. רבי יהודה בן בבא disapproves of slaughtering the calf on יום טוב to feed the raiding troop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lets us do food-making מלאכה on יום טוב only 'for you', meaning for Jews. Slaughtering for non-Jewish soldiers falls outside that permission. This is the line the גמרא will use to challenge רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: gain, what you got out of it
for you, and not for non-Jews

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה בן בבא answering שמעון התימני.

phrases.english: I wonder
if your gain was not cancelled out by your loss,
for the Torah said:
"For you" — and not for non-Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: תָּמֵהַּ אֲנִי אִם לֹא יָצָא שְׂכַרְכֶם בְּהֶפְסֵדְכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא brought in step 23 by giving its ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling allowing baking for soldiers on יום טוב (step 22)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids preparing food on יום טוב for non-Jewish soldiers, which sounds like it goes against רב הונא.

steps.title: Why forbidden? Jews could eat from the calf too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה בן בבא objected, since the calf was also fit for Jews to eat. That goes against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? It was fit to eat from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the challenge against רב הונא openly. If Jews could also eat from the calf, why was slaughtering it a sin?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said that if a Jew can get part of the food, all of it counts as fit for a Jew, so it may be made on יום טוב. The calf should be the same: Jews could eat some of it. Yet the ברייתא still calls it a sin, which seems to contradict רב הונא.

phrases.english: But why?
It was fit to eat from it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ruling of the ברייתא into a direct challenge to רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that food a Jew can share in may be made on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The calf was fit for Jews, just like the bread, yet the ברייתא forbids slaughtering it. So רב הונא's reasoning seems wrong.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the calf was a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the calf was a טרפה, which Jews may not eat. So it was made only for non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It was a טרפה calf.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends רב הונא by changing the facts of the story: the calf was a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה animal may not be eaten by a Jew. So nothing in this calf was fit for a Jew, and the whole slaughter was only for the soldiers. That case is different from רב הונא's bread, which Jews could eat.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal with a fatal defect, forbidden for a Jew to eat

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It was a טרפה calf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: עֵגֶל טְרֵפָה הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 by saying the calf was a טרפה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the calf was a טרפה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The calf was a regular kosher animal that Jews could eat, so the ברייתא contradicts רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The calf was a טרפה, fit only for non-Jews, so the ברייתא does not contradict רב הונא.

steps.title: But the טרפה calf was fit for dogs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: even a טרפה is fit for a Jew's dogs, so the slaughter could count as being for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was fit for dogs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף's answer. A טרפה can still be fed to dogs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If preparing food for animals counts as allowed on יום טוב, the calf was fit for something allowed: feeding dogs. Then why did רבי יהודה בן בבא call it a sin? The טרפה answer alone does not seem enough.

phrases.english: But it was fit for dogs!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's answer that the calf was a טרפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טרפה is still fit for dogs, so the slaughter could be seen as being for them, and should be allowed.

steps.title: Cooking for dogs is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that whether one may do מלאכה on יום טוב for dogs is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the dog question in short: this is a dispute between תנאים. The next step quotes the ברייתא that shows this dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone agrees that preparing food for animals is allowed on יום טוב. רבי יהודה בן בבא can hold the view that it is not allowed. Then the calf, fit only for soldiers and dogs, was truly forbidden, and רב הונא still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: it is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: It is a dispute of תנאים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the assumption behind the question is itself a dispute between תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that preparing food for dogs on יום טוב is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some תנאים forbid preparing food for dogs on יום טוב, and רבי יהודה בן בבא can follow them.

steps.title: The ברייתא: does 'every soul' include animals?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק 'that which is eaten by every soul'. 'Soul' could include animals, since animals are called 'soul' elsewhere, but the פסוק adds 'for you'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'Only that which is eaten by every soul, that alone may be done for you.' From the words 'every soul' I would think even an animal's soul is included, as it says: 'And one who kills the soul of an animal shall pay for it.' So the verse says 'for you'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא to prove there is a dispute about cooking for animals. Here we see the first side of it: the words 'for you' come to limit 'every soul'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נפש, 'soul', is used for animals in ויקרא, so 'every soul' could include animals. The word 'for you' narrows it, pointing toward people and not animals. The rest of the ברייתא, which shows the other opinion, continues next.

keyTerms.meaning: therefore the verse says (to teach otherwise)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the basis for the idea that יום טוב food permission is for people, not animals, which saves רבי יהודה בן בבא's ruling and keeps רב הונא standing.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
"Only that which is eaten by every soul,
that alone may be done for you,"
from what is implied by saying "every soul,"
I would understand
that even the soul of an animal is included,
as it is said:
"And one who kills the soul of an animal shall pay for it,"
Therefore the verse says "for you."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אַךְ אֲשֶׁר יֵאָכֵל לְכׇל נֶפֶשׁ הוּא לְבַדּוֹ יֵעָשֶׂה לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 28 that cooking for dogs is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That preparing food for animals on יום טוב is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'לְכׇל נֶפֶשׁ' and 'לָכֶם' in שמות 12:16, compared with ויקרא 24:18
